plan.title: bug(swarm): finalize-cohort fails after a correct sweep when the story was not launched by swarm:launch

narratives.Description: `swarm:finalize-cohort` moves the finished story briefs and then closes out the launch. For a story that was started in the session or by hand there is no launch record, so with a live session lease the close-out reports a failure although the move is correct, and the message does not say the move is on disk. Close-out also removes the registrations of every cohort the parent session launched and cannot close one story of a cohort. This story makes close-out work by story under one lock shared with `swarm:launch`, keeps the lease until every story of the session's records is closed, treats a story that no record lists as nothing to close out, makes a launch roll back only what it created, and makes a failure after the move say what is on disk.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker or orchestrator closing out a story, I want `swarm:finalize-cohort` to close out only the stories it completed and to exit 0 when no launch record lists them, so that a correct sweep never reads as a failure and closing one story never removes another story's registration or lease.

narratives.Overview:
1. Closed set. The closed set of a run is the stories that the sweep moved to a terminal folder in this run, or found already in `completed/` or `cancelled/`. A story that the sweep skipped for any other reason is not in the closed set. Close-out acts on the closed set only.
2. One lock. Close-out holds one lock for all of items 3 to 8. `swarm:launch` holds the same lock from before its occupancy claim or heartbeat until the launch can no longer retract its record or release the lease: through the record write, the optional `--output` write and every rollback path. Close-out does not hold the lock during the sweep.
3. Record read. Close-out reads every launch-occupancy record of the project root with a reader that keeps the `closed_story_ids` field and does not retract a record. When any record file cannot be read or parsed, close-out stops with a failure that names the file; it removes nothing and releases nothing.
4. Grouping. Each story of the closed set belongs to the launch-occupancy record that lists it, or to no record. When the closed set has stories of more than one record, close-out stops with a failure that names the stories of each record; it removes nothing and releases nothing.
5. Stories in no record. For a story of the closed set that no record lists, close-out removes nothing and releases nothing. When a worker assignment record with that `story_id` exists, it prints one line that names the story and that record's `dispatch_id` and says the record was left in place. A run whose closed set has only such stories exits 0.
6. Stories in one record. For the stories of the closed set that one record lists, when the record's session is the live lease holder, the ambient-session check of today runs and refuses as today. Then close-out removes the assignment records whose `dispatch_id` is the record's session and whose `story_id` is in the closed set, and adds those stories to `closed_story_ids` in the record. The record's `story_ids` and cohort key are not changed. A record without the field reads as an empty list. All of this item applies only when the record's session is the live lease holder. When it is not, and the record was not already fully closed before this run, the result is today's and close-out removes no assignment and marks no story: with another session as the live holder the run refuses; with no live lease the run does not fail. Stories that become terminal in this run do not make such a record fully closed.
7. Lease last. When every story of every launch-occupancy record of that session is in its `closed_story_ids` and that session is the live lease holder, close-out releases the launcher occupancy lease and then removes those records. When the release fails, the records stay and the run fails.
8. Finish after release. A launch-occupancy record whose stories were all in `closed_story_ids` before this run and whose session is not the live lease holder is removed, and no lease is released for it. This is how a run that released the lease and then stopped is finished by running the command again, also after another session took the lease.
9. Other readers. `resolveLaunchOccupancySessionId` and the record parser keep `closed_story_ids` when they read and write a record. The record write in `swarm:launch` keeps its roster guard unchanged.
10. Launch rollback. When `swarm:launch` writes a worker assignment record for a destination that already has one, an identical record is kept as it is and a different one is refused before anything is overwritten (the #6334 no-re-pointing rule). A launch rolls back only the assignment records, the launch-occupancy record and the lease that this attempt created; the assignment writer's own failure cleanup keeps a record that existed before the attempt.
11. Failure text. When close-out fails after the sweep moved a file, the text output and the `--json` output say that the lifecycle move is on disk and must be committed, and list the source path and the destination path of each brief moved in this run. The exit code is 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a story that was not launched by `swarm:launch`, a live session occupancy lease and no launch-occupancy record, when `swarm:finalize-cohort` completes the sweep, then it exits 0, reports no missing close-out record and the lease is still held.
- Given two linked worktrees, a terminal copy of story S in the first with no launch record there, and a worker assignment record for S written by a launch in the second, when finalize runs in the first, then that assignment record remains, one line names it and the exit code is 0.
- Given a launch-occupancy record file that cannot be parsed, when close-out runs, then it fails, names the file, removes no assignment and releases no lease.
- Given a cohort of two stories, when finalize closes one story, then only that story's assignment record is removed, the record lists it in `closed_story_ids` and the launcher lease is still held.
- Given the last open story of a cohort, when finalize closes it, then the launcher lease is released and the record is removed.
- Given two launch cohorts of one parent session, when one cohort is closed out, then the other cohort's assignment records remain and the lease is still held.
- Given the last open story and a lease release that fails, when the run ends, then it exits 1 and the record remains; when the same command runs again and the release succeeds, then the lease is released and the record is removed.
- Given a run that released the lease and stopped before it removed the record, when the same command runs again, then the record is removed, no lease is released and the exit code is 0.
- Given that same stopped run and another session that has since taken the lease, when the same command runs again, then the record is removed and the other session's lease is still held.
- Given a session with two fully closed records, a release that succeeded and a removal that stopped after the first record, when the same command runs again, then the second record is removed.
- Given a launch that has claimed the lease and written its assignment records but not yet its launch-occupancy record, when a close-out of the session's last closed cohort runs at the same time, then the close-out waits for the lock, finds the new record and does not release the lease.
- Given launch A that wrote its launch-occupancy record and then fails its `--output` write, and launch B of the same session that started after A's record write, then B's lease claim waits for A's rollback, and after both end B's record, assignments and lease are in place.
- Given a successful launch A whose worker is active, when the same session repeats that launch as B and B fails its `--output` write, then A's assignment record, launch-occupancy record and lease are all still in place.
- Given a record that lists stories A and B with only A in `closed_story_ids`, another session as the live lease holder and B terminal, when close-out runs for B, then it refuses, removes no assignment and does not add B to `closed_story_ids`.
- Given a cohort whose other story was cancelled and swept as terminal, when the last completed story is closed, then the lease is released.
- Given a requested story that the sweep skipped because it is in neither an active nor a terminal folder, when close-out runs, then that story's assignment record and its place in the record are unchanged and the lease is still held.
- Given a closed set with stories of two launch-occupancy records, when close-out runs, then it fails, names the stories of each record, and removes and releases nothing.
- Given a story launched by `swarm:launch` whose record has an open story and names a session that is not the live lease holder, when close-out runs, then it refuses as today.
- Given two close-outs of different stories of one cohort that run at the same time, then both stories end in `closed_story_ids`.
- Given a record with `closed_story_ids`, when `resolveLaunchOccupancySessionId` reads and rewrites it, then the field is kept.
- Given a close-out step that fails after the sweep moved files, then the text output and the JSON output say that the move is on disk and list the source and destination path of each moved brief.
narratives.Constraint:
- Removing a worker assignment record because its `story_id` matches, without a local launch-occupancy record whose session is its `dispatch_id` (comment 6933796119 finding 1).
- A lock that covers only the record write of a launch, or that ends at the record write (comment 6933796119 finding 2; comment 6933858394 finding 1).
- A launch rollback that removes a registration the attempt did not create (comment 6933917640 finding 1).
- Counting stories that become terminal in this run toward a fully closed record when the record's session does not hold the lease (comment 6933858394 finding 2).
- Removing the record before the release, or refusing a fully closed record after the release (comment 6933727544 finding 2; comment 6933796119 finding 3).
- Treating "no record lists these stories" as proof that nothing was launched (comment 6933727544 finding 1).
- Counting a skipped story as closed (comment 6933727544 finding 3).
- Closing stories of several records in one run; an automatic collector for abandoned stories; close-out by recomputed worktree path.

## In plain English
`swarm:finalize-cohort` moves the finished story briefs to their final folder and then closes out the launch: it removes the worker registrations and releases the launcher's lease. For a story that was started in the session or by hand, there is no launch record. When the session holds a live lease, the close-out step reports "occupancy record is missing or belongs to a different cohort" and the command fails, although the briefs were moved correctly. The message does not say that the move is on disk, so workers commit it by hand and guess. A second problem was accepted on #6334 and moved here by the operator: close-out removes the registrations of every cohort the parent launched, and it cannot close one story of a cohort. The recommended fix treats "no launch record names these stories" as nothing to close out, closes out by story, and makes a failure after the move say what is on disk.

## Pains
- P1 — For a story that was not launched by `swarm:launch`, with a live session occupancy lease, `swarm:finalize-cohort` reports a failure and exits non-zero after a correct sweep.
- P2 — When a close-out step fails after the sweep wrote files, the output does not say that the lifecycle move is on disk or what to commit.
- P3 — Close-out removes the registrations of every cohort the parent session launched and cannot close part of a cohort (#6334 lean 6908164963 item 4; folded here by comment 6924272310).

## Constraints (not pains)
- A story launched by `swarm:launch` whose close-out record belongs to a different cohort or session still refuses to release that lease (issue Acceptance Criterion 2).
- Close-out matches on the recorded `dispatch_id` and `story_id`, never on a recomputed worktree path (#6334 Reject list).

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/swarm/complete-cohort.ts` 739-745: the sweep runs first. 747-770: with a live occupancy lease and a lookup result other than `ok`, the run sets `ok = false` with "swarm close-out occupancy record is missing or belongs to a different cohort". 777-785: `cleanupWorkerAuthAssignmentsForDispatch` is called with the session id only. 786-798: the launcher lease is released. 800-814: exit 1 when `ok` is false; the text does not mention the sweep.
- `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts` 1337-1388 `resolveLaunchOccupancySessionId`: returns `missing` when no record has exactly this story set, and `wrong-cohort` when records disagree or the recorded session does not match. A subset of a record's stories is `missing`.
- Issue comment 6924272310: the scope addition and its three added Acceptance Criteria.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- F1. Not launched is not a failure. When no launch-occupancy record lists any story of the closed set, close-out has nothing to remove and nothing to release. The run stays `ok`, exits 0 and prints one line that says no launch record names these stories.
- F2. Close-out by story. When the closed set equals, or is a subset of, the stories of one launch-occupancy record, close-out removes the assignment records whose `dispatch_id` matches that record's session and whose `story_id` is in the closed set, and removes those stories from the record.
- F3. Lease last. The launcher occupancy lease is released only when no launch-occupancy record of that session still lists a story.
- F4. Refusals kept. A record whose session does not match the live lease or the ambient session (`wrong-cohort`, ambient-owner conflict) refuses as today. A closed set that mixes stories of two records, or listed and unlisted stories, refuses and names the stories of each record.
- F5. Failure text. When any close-out step fails after the sweep moved files, the output says that the lifecycle move is on disk, lists the moved paths, and says that they must be committed. The exit code stays 1.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is F1 safe? Can "no record lists these stories" also be true for a story that `swarm:launch` did launch (for example after a record was retracted), so that a lease or a registration stays behind without a message?
2. Is the refusal in F4 for a mixed set right, or should close-out handle each record in turn?
3. Does F3 leave a lease held for ever when a story of a cohort is cancelled or never closed?

## In plain English

The command can finish moving story briefs and then report failure because it cannot identify a launch to close. It also removes too many worker registrations when several launches share one parent session.

The proposed direction is sound, but F1–F3 need changes before this design can bind. Missing launch records do not prove that nothing remains to clean up. Removing stories from those records also needs a retry rule: otherwise a failed lease release can become an apparent success on the next attempt.

Answers to the Stop 1 questions:

1. **F1 is not safe as an unconditional success rule.** Existing code can erase launch records while worker registrations remain, and unreadable records disappear from lookup results.
2. **F4’s mixed-set refusal is a reasonable first ship.** It avoids introducing a multi-record transaction. The refusal should identify each group and allow separate retries without losing already-finished work.
3. **F3 can leave close-out unfinished for an abandoned story.** A cancelled story can already be passed through the sweep as terminal; a never-closed story needs an explicit terminal disposition. The lease is not necessarily live forever because occupancy has expiry checks.

Evidence below was read with `git show` at `aab2f7971f3d015118b6e07d34127df2ea5dbd1c`. No tests, builds, mutations, or external posts were performed.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Absence of a launch record does not establish absence of cleanup obligations

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:1189–1217` converts unreadable or malformed records into null or skips them. At `1352–1355` and `1380–1385`, lookup retracts records when occupancy is no longer live. Launch rollback at `1905–1925` continues to retract the launch record even if worker-assignment removal fails. Worker assignments are stored separately and cleaned through `packages/core/src/swarm/worker-auth-assignment.ts:809–868`.

**Failure mode:** A launched story retains an assignment after rollback failure or lease expiry, but lookup reports no launch record. F1 then exits successfully without cleaning that assignment. Its informational line reports absence, but conceals the unresolved obligation. An unreadable remaining-cohort record could also be omitted from F3’s count, permitting premature lease release.

**Disposition consequence:** F1 needs a distinction between verified absence and unreadable, retracted, or contradictory state. A narrow check of existing worker assignments by recorded story identity can detect residue; it must not infer release authority from that residue. Uncertain records must not count as empty for F3. This does not require recreating launch history.

### 2. blocks-the-design — Removing membership before lease release loses retry ownership

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/swarm/complete-cohort.ts:777–797` performs assignment cleanup before release and permits release to fail. `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:1145–1159` derives record identity from the original story set, while `1266–1269` rejects changing the roster of an existing live record. Worker-auth cleanup has its own lock at `worker-auth-assignment.ts:824–868`; the launch-record persistence path at `launch.ts:1234–1277` does not share that transaction.

**Failure mode:** Under F2, the last story is removed from the record; F3 then fails to release the lease. A retry finds no record listing that story and takes F1’s success path, leaving the lease behind. Concurrent partial closes can also read the same roster and overwrite one another’s removals unless the new update operation serializes them.

**Disposition consequence:** F2–F3 need one explicit, retryable close-out state transition: preserve the original cohort identity and enough ownership evidence to retry a pending release, and serialize remaining-story updates and the last-story decision with competing launch/close-out operations. Problem: `swarm:finalize-cohort` moves the finished story briefs and then closes out the launch. For each launch record it removes the registrations of those stories and marks them closed in the record; the record keeps its original story list. The lease is released only when every story of every record of that session is marked closed and every record could be read, and the records are removed only after the release succeeded, so a failed release is retried by running the command again. Any failure after the briefs were moved says that the move is on disk and lists each moved brief.

- It does not collect abandoned stories. A story stays open in its record until it is completed or cancelled.
- It does not release a lease that another session or cohort holds; those refusals stay as today.

2. One lock. Close-out does not hold the lock during the sweep.
3. Record read. Close-out reads every launch-occupancy record of the project root with a reader that keeps the `closed_story_ids` field and does not retract a record. When any record file cannot be read or parsed, close-out stops with a failure that names the file; it removes nothing and releases nothing.
4. Grouping. Each story of the closed set belongs to the launch-occupancy record that lists it, or to no record. When the closed set has stories of more than one record, close-out stops with a failure that names the stories of each record; it removes nothing and releases nothing.
5. Stories in no record. For a story of the closed set that no record lists, close-out removes nothing and releases nothing. When a worker assignment record with that `story_id` exists, it prints one line that names the story and that record's `dispatch_id` and says the record was left in place. A run whose closed set has only such stories exits 0.
6. Stories in one record. For the stories of the closed set that one record lists, when the record's session is the live lease holder, the ambient-session check of today runs and refuses as today. Then close-out removes the assignment records whose `dispatch_id` is the record's session and whose `story_id` is in the closed set, and adds those stories to `closed_story_ids` in the record. The record's `story_ids` and cohort key are not changed. A record without the field reads as an empty list. All of this item applies only when the record's session is the live lease holder. When it is not, and the record was not already fully closed before this run, the result is today's and close-out removes no assignment and marks no story: with another session as the live holder the run refuses; with no live lease the run does not fail. Stories that become terminal in this run do not make such a record fully closed.
7. Lease last. When every story of every launch-occupancy record of that session is in its `closed_story_ids` and that session is the live lease holder, close-out releases the launcher occupancy lease and then removes those records. When the release fails, the records stay and the run fails.
8. Finish after release. A launch-occupancy record whose stories were all in `closed_story_ids` before this run and whose session is not the live lease holder is removed, and no lease is released for it. What it does not do:
- It does not remove a registration for a story that no local launch record lists. It reports it, because another launcher in a linked worktree may own it.
- It does not close stories of two launch records in one run. It refuses that and names the stories of each record.

## Bound remedy
1. Closed set. The closed set of a run is the stories that the sweep moved to a terminal folder in this run, or found already in `completed/` or `cancelled/`. A story that the sweep skipped for any other reason is not in the closed set. Close-out acts on the closed set only.
2. One lock. Close-out holds one lock for all of items 3 to 8. `swarm:launch` holds the same lock from before its occupancy claim or heartbeat until the launch can no longer retract its record or release the lease: through the record write, the optional `--output` write and every rollback path. Close-out does not hold the lock during the sweep.
3. Record read. Close-out reads every launch-occupancy record of the project root with a reader that keeps the `closed_story_ids` field and does not retract a record. When any record file cannot be read or parsed, close-out stops with a failure that names the file; it removes nothing and releases nothing.
4. Grouping. Each story of the closed set belongs to the launch-occupancy record that lists it, or to no record. When the closed set has stories of more than one record, close-out stops with a failure that names the stories of each record; it removes nothing and releases nothing.
5. Stories in no record. For a story of the closed set that no record lists, close-out removes nothing and releases nothing. When a worker assignment record with that `story_id` exists, it prints one line that names the story and that record's `dispatch_id` and says the record was left in place. A run whose closed set has only such stories exits 0.
6. Stories in one record. For the stories of the closed set that one record lists, when the record's session is the live lease holder, the ambient-session check of today runs and refuses as today. Then close-out removes the assignment records whose `dispatch_id` is the record's session and whose `story_id` is in the closed set, and adds those stories to `closed_story_ids` in the record. The record's `story_ids` and cohort key are not changed. A record without the field reads as an empty list. All of this item applies only when the record's session is the live lease holder. When it is not, and the record was not already fully closed before this run, the result is today's and close-out removes no assignment and marks no story: with another session as the live holder the run refuses; with no live lease the run does not fail. Stories that become terminal in this run do not make such a record fully closed.
7. Lease last. When every story of every launch-occupancy record of that session is in its `closed_story_ids` and that session is the live lease holder, close-out releases the launcher occupancy lease and then removes those records. When the release fails, the records stay and the run fails.
8. Finish after release. A launch-occupancy record whose stories were all in `closed_story_ids` before this run and whose session is not the live lease holder is removed, and no lease is released for it. This is how a run that released the lease and then stopped is finished by running the command again, also after another session took the lease.
9. Other readers. `resolveLaunchOccupancySessionId` and the record parser keep `closed_story_ids` when they read and write a record. The record write in `swarm:launch` keeps its roster guard unchanged.
10. Launch rollback. When `swarm:launch` writes a worker assignment record for a destination that already has one, an identical record is kept as it is and a different one is refused before anything is overwritten (the #6334 no-re-pointing rule). A launch rolls back only the assignment records, the launch-occupancy record and the lease that this attempt created; the assignment writer's own failure cleanup keeps a record that existed before the attempt.
11. Failure text. When close-out fails after the sweep moved a file, the text output and the `--json` output say that the lifecycle move is on disk and must be committed, and list the source path and the destination path of each brief moved in this run. The exit code is 1.

- Given a story that was not launched by `swarm:launch`, a live session occupancy lease and no launch-occupancy record, when `swarm:finalize-cohort` completes the sweep, then it exits 0, reports no missing close-out record and the lease is still held.
- Given two linked worktrees, a terminal copy of story S in the first with no launch record there, and a worker assignment record for S written by a launch in the second, when finalize runs in the first, then that assignment record remains, one line names it and the exit code is 0.
- Given a launch-occupancy record file that cannot be parsed, when close-out runs, then it fails, names the file, removes no assignment and releases no lease.
- Given a cohort of two stories, when finalize closes one story, then only that story's assignment record is removed, the record lists it in `closed_story_ids` and the launcher lease is still held.
- Given the last open story of a cohort, when finalize closes it, then the launcher lease is released and the record is removed.
- Given two launch cohorts of one parent session, when one cohort is closed out, then the other cohort's assignment records remain and the lease is still held.
- Given the last open story and a lease release that fails, when the run ends, then it exits 1 and the record remains; when the same command runs again and the release succeeds, then the lease is released and the record is removed.
- Given a run that released the lease and stopped before it removed the record, when the same command runs again, then the record is removed, no lease is released and the exit code is 0.
- Given that same stopped run and another session that has since taken the lease, when the same command runs again, then the record is removed and the other session's lease is still held.
- Given a session with two fully closed records, a release that succeeded and a removal that stopped after the first record, when the same command runs again, then the second record is removed.
- Given a launch that has claimed the lease and written its assignment records but not yet its launch-occupancy record, when a close-out of the session's last closed cohort runs at the same time, then the close-out waits for the lock, finds the new record and does not release the lease.
- Given launch A that wrote its launch-occupancy record and then fails its `--output` write, and launch B of the same session that started after A's record write, then B's lease claim waits for A's rollback, and after both end B's record, assignments and lease are in place.

- Given a record that lists stories A and B with only A in `closed_story_ids`, another session as the live lease holder and B terminal, when close-out runs for B, then it refuses, removes no assignment and does not add B to `closed_story_ids`.
- Given a cohort whose other story was cancelled and swept as terminal, when the last completed story is closed, then the lease is released.
- Given a requested story that the sweep skipped because it is in neither an active nor a terminal folder, when close-out runs, then that story's assignment record and its place in the record are unchanged and the lease is still held.
- Given a closed set with stories of two launch-occupancy records, when close-out runs, then it fails, names the stories of each record, and removes and releases nothing.
- Given a story launched by `swarm:launch` whose record has an open story and names a session that is not the live lease holder, when close-out runs, then it refuses as today.
- Given two close-outs of different stories of one cohort that run at the same time, then both stories end in `closed_story_ids`.
- Given a record with `closed_story_ids`, when `resolveLaunchOccupancySessionId` reads and rewrites it, then the field is kept.

## In plain English

Problem: `swarm:finalize-cohort` moves the finished story briefs and then closes out the launch. For a story that was started in the session or by hand there was no launch record, and when the session held a live lease the command reported a failure although the briefs were moved correctly. The message did not say that the move was on disk. Close-out also removed the registrations of every cohort the parent session launched, and it could not close one story of a cohort.

Accepted solution: close-out works by story. The stories it closes are only those the sweep completed or found already completed or cancelled. For the launch record that lists them, it removes the registrations of those stories that carry that record's session and marks the stories closed in the record, which keeps its original story list. The lease is released only when every story of every record of that session is marked closed, and records are removed after the release. A record that was already fully closed and whose session no longer holds the lease is removed with no release, so an interrupted run can be finished by running the command again. A story that no record lists is not a failure: the command exits 0, and a registration found for it is reported and left in place. A launch holds the same lock as close-out from its lease claim until it can no longer undo its work, and its rollback removes only what that attempt created. Any failure after the briefs were moved says that the move is on disk and lists the source and destination of each moved brief.

Limits accepted: close-out refuses a run that mixes stories of two launch records; it does not collect abandoned stories; it does not remove a registration that no local launch record covers. `swarm:launch` changes in two places only: how long it holds the shared lock and what its rollback removes. The design adds one field to the launch record and one shared lock, and no new check or approval. It was checked by reading the source at the pinned commit; no code was run. No leftover next-build.

## Problem

`swarm:finalize-cohort` moves the briefs, then reports a failure, when the story was not launched by `swarm:launch`.

In `packages/core/src/swarm/complete-cohort.ts` (origin/master e32e58147), the sweep runs first (`sweepCohortWithArgs`, line 739). Then, at lines 747-765, if `readOccupancy` finds a live occupancy lease (for example the one `session:start` takes) and `resolveLaunchOccupancySessionId` (`packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts` 1333) finds no launch occupancy record for the story set, the run sets `ok = false` with "swarm close-out occupancy record is missing or belongs to a different cohort". A story dispatched in-session or by hand has no launch record, so this branch always fires for it.

The CLI exits 1 (line 808); through `task` the shell sees 201. The lifecycle move is already on disk, so workers commit the sweep by hand. The message does not say that the sweep succeeded.

Related: #6334 item 6 (partial close-out needs the exact story set). This issue is the case with no launch record at all.

## Evidence

- 2026-11-16, #6205: completion #6387 after finalize reported the error.
- 2026-11-16, #6398: completion #6403 (f44c44920); finalize exited 201 after a correct sweep; the worker committed the sweep.
- 2026-11-16, #6333: completion #6415 (e32e58147); same error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a story that was not launched by `swarm:launch` and a live session occupancy lease, when `swarm:finalize-cohort` completes the sweep, then it exits 0 and does not report a missing close-out record.
- Given a story that was launched by `swarm:launch`, when its close-out record belongs to a different cohort, then `swarm:finalize-cohort` still refuses to release that lease.
- Given a close-out step that fails after the sweep wrote files, when the run ends, then the output says that the lifecycle move is on disk and what to commit.
